title: Klarna: The Deserved Downfall Of A $45B Predatory App
summary: Explainer connecting Klarna's consumer-harm lawsuits to its post-IPO stock decline and credit-loss disclosures.

assertions.quote: Klarna's automated withdrawals hit users when their balances were low, triggering insufficient funds and overdraft fees
Klarna approves purchasing power without investigating ability to pay, replacing underwriting with direct access to pull payments

verdicts.note: This is an allegation made in litigation, not yet a proven fact, though consistent with the industry's generally light underwriting.

NBER's analysis of a merchant's own BNPL lending function finds that customers with high credit scores, and those interested in high-profit-margin products, are more likely to be approved -- showing approval does weigh creditworthiness.

assertions.quote: users take out several at once across different apps, and the providers don't check one another
the interest can run as high as roughly 36%
it reported a 102% year-over-year spike in its provision for credit losses

verdicts.note: A major lender's own quarterly earnings disclosures reported a large year-over-year increase in credit-loss provisions after its IPO.
